question: What is the primary focus when treating a family as a unit of care?

options.A: The health and well-being of the entire household
options.B: The medical history of the oldest relative
options.C: The financial status of the parents
options.D: The physical health of the breadwinner alone

explanation: Treating the family as a unit means looking beyond a single patient to address how health issues affect all household members. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why does a nurse assess family dynamics during primary health care visits?

options.A: To decide which relative should pay the hospital bills
options.B: To report family conflicts to local community leaders
options.C: To isolate the sick member from the rest of the home
options.D: To understand how illness impacts household stability and daily routines

explanation: Illness in one person disrupts the whole system, so nurses evaluate dynamics to see how daily life and caregiving are affected. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which family structure consists of one man married to multiple wives?
explanation: A polygamous family structure features multiple spouses under one overall family unit, which is prevalent in various Nigerian communities. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h2)

question: A patient lives with parents, grandparents, and uncles under one roof. What structure is this?
explanation: The presence of multiple generations living together or closely linked defines the extended family network. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main developmental task of a beginning family stage?

options.A: Providing care for frail elderly grandparents
options.B: Managing teenagers leaving the house for university
options.C: Coping with the retirement of both spouses
options.D: Establishing a stable home for a newly married couple

explanation: The beginning stage focuses on the couple adjusting to life together and setting up their household before children arrive. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h3)

question: During which family life cycle stage do parents typically face the challenge of launching children?

options.A: When young adults leave home for work or school
options.B: When elderly relatives move in due to chronic illness
options.C: When the couple first gets married without kids
options.D: When infants receive their first routine immunizations

explanation: The launching stage occurs as growing children transition out of the family home into independent adult roles. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h3)

question: Socio-cultural and economic factors in Nigerian families primarily influence what aspect of health?

options.A: The genetic makeup of newborn babies
options.B: The number of children born in a generation
options.C: The physical layout of primary health clinics

explanation: Beliefs and finances guide how and when families decide to seek medical help for an illness. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why might a family try home remedies before visiting a clinic?

options.A: Modern medications are completely unavailable in all urban areas
options.B: Primary health nurses instruct them to stay away from hospitals
options.C: Economic constraints and cultural traditions influence initial responses
options.D: Government policies forbid treating common infections at clinics

explanation: Financial limitations and deeply rooted traditions often lead families to explore local or traditional options first. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a family genogram in nursing?

options.A: To map the family's financial income and expenditure records
options.B: To evaluate the structural layout of the family kitchen
options.C: To record medical history and hereditary conditions across generations
options.D: To track the daily school attendance of school-aged children

explanation: A genogram uses family tree symbols to track health conditions and genetic patterns over multiple generations. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which assessment tool specifically examines a family's connections with external systems like church and work?
explanation: The ecogram illustrates how the household interacts with outside social and community environments. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common sign of family dysfunction?

options.B: Domestic violence and frequent severe conflict
options.C: Neglect of vulnerable children and elderly relatives
options.D: Open and supportive communication among members

explanation: Healthy communication is a sign of a functional family, whereas abuse, neglect, and conflict indicate dysfunction. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a frequent consequence of role overload in a caregiving family member?

options.A: Improved financial status for the entire household
options.C: Faster recovery of the chronically ill patient
options.D: Physical exhaustion and burnout from carrying all burdens

explanation: When one person handles all caregiving and financial tasks alone, they often suffer from severe fatigue and stress. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a core responsibility of a nurse practicing family-centered care?

options.A: Isolating patients from their relatives during treatment
options.B: Making final legal decisions on behalf of family members
options.C: Financially supporting impoverished households out of pocket
options.D: Acting as an educator, advocate, and counselor for the household

explanation: Nurses support families by educating them on health, advocating for their needs, and counseling them through crises. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is building trust essential for community health nurses working with families?

options.A: It allows the nurse to take over household financial management
options.B: It encourages open dialogue and willingness to adopt health recommendations
options.C: It legally binds the family to follow hospital instructions
options.D: It prevents family members from seeking traditional medicine ever again

explanation: Trust enables families to share sensitive issues and accept guidance from the nurse without fear of judgment. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h7)
